items.title: State of emergency is no ‘magic wand’ for galamsey – Lands Ministry
items.description: The Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources has cautioned against presenting a state of emergency as a quick solution to Ghana’s persistent illegal mining crisis, popularly known as galamsey. The Ministry’s spokesperson, Paa Kwesi Schandorf, said. However, a state of emergency could lead to tighter restrictions on mining and increased security operations in affected communities; it would not automatically resolve the factors driving illegal mining. He argued that the government must first establish what additional impact such a declaration would have before considering the measure, particularly given the interventions already being undertaken to combat illegal mining. Mr Schandorf noted that some of the restrictions and heightened security measures that could accompany a state of emergency were already being implemented in galamsey-affected areas through ongoing operations. “We should be careful not to consistently indicate or project a state of emergency as a certain magic wand, if once implemented, would automatically transform our fortunes,” he said. He stressed that declaring a state of emergency could have wider consequences for communities, including restrictions on economic activities, and should therefore be based on a clear assessment of its necessity and likely outcomes. Mr Schandorf also pointed to the work of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), saying several measures being pursued by the government were already aimed at disrupting illegal mining activities and protecting the environment. “I’m not equating the state of emergency to NAIMOS intervention. I’m just saying that we should be careful not to consistently project that as that magic wand that will transform our fortunes,” he explained. According to him, President John Dramani Mahama has indicated that any decision to declare a state of emergency would be informed by security assessments and taken when circumstances warrant it. Mr Schandorf therefore said there was currently no immediate justification for such a declaration, given the measures being implemented by the government and security agencies. He said the debate should instead focus on identifying the specific additional benefits a state of emergency would provide and whether those benefits would significantly improve the fight against illegal mining beyond the interventions already underway.

items.title: Bringing 10 bags of clothes as gifts? Customs explains when duties may apply
items.description: Revenue Officer at Accra International Airport Preventive Unit Conrad Attu has said travellers arriving in Ghana with multiple bags of new clothing and other items intended as gifts for family and friends could be required to pay customs duties. Mr Attu explained that passengers are required to declare goods they are bringing into the country as gifts, noting that the quantity and nature of the items could determine whether customs duties apply. “Once you are stating they are gifts, and gifts now are dutiable, once they are dutiable, another thing we will consider is the value as to the quantity you are carrying and also whether the items are identical and are similar in nature,” he said. The clarification is particularly relevant to travellers who return to Ghana with large quantities of clothing for relatives and friends. Speaking at JoyFM Super Morning Show on September 1, Mr Attu acknowledged that it is common for passengers to carry items for loved ones but said the quantity involved could raise questions. “With the clothing you mentioned, there are times that you see people carry, let’s say, one bag full of clothing, all new,” he explained. “You get people saying these are for my family, for my friends. Yes, we understand. But you may buy just one bag, another person may buy 10 bags,” he added. According to Customs, the fact that goods are intended as gifts does not automatically exempt them from duties. Officers will consider the value and quantity of the goods, as well as whether the items are identical or similar, before determining if any concessional allowance applies. Mr Attu also addressed what he described as a misconception among some travellers that paying for air freight or excess baggage means no additional customs charges will be required. “There’s a misconception where people also think that once I have bought the items and I’ve paid for the air freight, paid for excess luggage where need be, there’s no point where I have to pay duties on these items,” he said. “But there’s a difference between paying tax on the items and also paying for your excess luggage for it to be carried by the airline,” he stressed. Meanwhile, he explained that passenger profiling forms part of the customs clearance process. “When you get to the officer who is profiling, he would ask you one or two questions as part of the procedure,” he said. The questions may relate to a traveller’s itinerary or travel history, while officers may also request passports to verify travel information. “Most often, we request for the passport too, confirm your travel itinerary,” Mr Attu explained. Passengers are also expected to complete the required written declarations, either through forms provided during the flight or upon arrival. The Customs Division is therefore urging travellers to properly declare goods being brought into Ghana and to understand that baggage or freight charges paid to an airline are separate from any customs duties that may be assessed on the goods.

items.title: FG expands national tertiary institutions’ ranking, makes participation compulsory
items.description: The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has expanded Nigeria’s national tertiary education ranking framework to cover universities, polytechnics and colleges of education. ‎This is contained in a statement issued on Tuesday in Abuja by Mr Ikharo Attah, Special Adviser to the Minister on Media and Communications. ‎Attah quoted Alausa to have announced the development at a meeting with the Nigerian Universities Ranking Advisory Committee (NURAC), adding that participation was now compulsory for all tertiary institutions. ‎Alausa said the expanded ranking framework was part of President Bola Tinubu’s education reforms under the Renewed Hope Agenda, implemented through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI). ‎According to him, the initiative is aimed at strengthening quality, accountability, institutional performance and global competitiveness across Nigeria’s tertiary education system. ‎“The ranking will provide institutions with clear benchmarks for assessing their performance, identifying areas requiring improvement and measuring progress, while promoting healthy competition and continuous institutional advancement,” he said. ‎Alausa said that the 2026/2027 ranking exercise for universities would commence in September, while the committee would determine the appropriate timeline for extending the exercise to polytechnics and colleges of education. ‎He added that the Federal Government would provide funding for the exercise through the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund). The minister added that TETFund would develop guidelines to institutionalise the ranking and formally communicate to vice-chancellors and heads of other tertiary institutions that participation was compulsory. ‎He reassured the committee of the ministry’s commitment to providing the policy direction, funding and capacity-building support required to make the ranking exercise credible, sustainable and impactful. “The ministry will work with the committee to facilitate in-service training and institutional capacity-building programmes across tertiary institutions, with the expectation that significantly more Nigerian institutions will achieve greater global recognition in subsequent international ranking exercises,” Alausa said. ‎Alausa reiterated the commitment of the Federal Ministry of Education to ensure that the ranking framework became a credible tool for driving quality, accountability and continuous improvement in Nigeria’s tertiary education sector. ‎On her part, the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Ahmad, described the initiative as a significant step toward strengthening accountability and quality across the tertiary education system. ‎Ahmad said healthy competition was essential to encourage institutions to assess their performance, address identified gaps and consistently improve the quality of education they provide. ‎“Ranking should cover both public and private institutions, as this will provide a mechanism for establishing and maintaining minimum standards across the sector,” she said. ‎Ahmad assured the committee of the ministry’s full support, saying the exercise would help institutions understand their strengths and weaknesses and drive measurable improvements as the nation’s tertiary education system continued to expand. ‎Also, Emeritus Prof. Peter Okebukola, Chairman of NURAC, congratulated President Tinubu on the increasing number of Nigerian universities gaining global recognition. ‎Okebukola, also the former Executive Secretary of the National Universities Commission (NUC), called for greater investment in university education to accelerate the progress. ‎“The committee’s mandate has now been expanded to cover polytechnics and colleges of education, leading to its transformation into the Nigerian Tertiary Education Ranking Advisory Committee,” he said. ‎Okebukola expressed optimism that sustained investment, stronger institutional capacity and the new national ranking framework would enable more Nigerian institutions to make significant progress in international rankings. ‎He said the initiative would also enable Nigerian tertiary institutions to compete more confidently with leading institutions globally. ‎( NAN ) The post FG expands national tertiary institutions’ ranking, makes participation compulsory appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Zoundwéogo/Sport: Béré s’adjuge la coupe du haut-commissaire face à Gom-Boussougou
items.description: BURKINA-ZOUNDWEOGO-SPORT-COUPE Zoundwéogo/Sport: Béré s’adjuge la coupe du haut-commissaire face à Gom-Boussougou Manga, 29 août 2026 (AIB)- L’équipe de Béré a remporté, samedi, la deuxième édition de la Coupe du haut-commissaire de la province du Zoundwéogo, en s’imposant face à Gom-Boussougou sur le score de 2 buts à 1, au terme de la finale disputée entre les deux équipes. Placée sous le thème « Par le sport, consolidons la cohésion sociale et la solidarité pour un Zoundwéogo uni et résilient », la compétition a réuni les équipes représentant les différentes communes de la province. Grâce à cette victoire, Béré repart avec une enveloppe de 200 000 F CFA, un jeu de maillots, des médailles et le trophée m. Malgré sa défaite, Gom-Boussougou a opposé une belle résistance à son adversaire jusqu’au coup de sifflet final. Au-delà de l’enjeu sportif, cette compétition a constitué un cadre de retrouvailles et de renforcement de la cohésion entre les filles et fils des différentes communes du Zoundwéogo, dans un esprit d’unité et de solidarité. La patronne de cette deuxième édition, la gouverneure de la région du Nazinon, Massadalo Yvette Nacoulma/Sanou, s’est réjouie de la tenue de la compétition. « Béré a certes remporté la victoire, mais en définitive, c’est l’ensemble de la province qui sort gagnant », a-t-elle déclaré. Elle a souligné que cette coupe vise à « promouvoir la cohésion sociale, le mieux-vivre ensemble et, partant, le développement de la province du Zoundwéogo et de l’ensemble de la région du Nazinon ». Pour le promoteur de la compétition, le haut-commissaire du Zoundwéogo, Julien Ouédraogo, cette initiative sportive vise à « rapprocher davantage les fils et filles de la province et de la région, car sans cohésion sociale, on ne peut rien faire ». Le capitaine de Béré, Soumaïla Zoundi, a, pour sa part, dédié le trophée à l’ensemble des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) pour leur engagement dans la défense de la patrie. Agence d’Information du Burkina SM/BGB/bak

items.title: Precious Mawunya-ko appointed PRO for 5th Praise Achievement Awards
items.description: The Board and Executive Management of the Praise Achievement Awards have officially announced the appointment of astute media personality, brand strategist and talent manager Precious Mawunya-ko, popularly known as SOG Precious, as the Public Relations Officer (PRO) for the upcoming 5th edition of the prestigious awards scheme. Precious steps into the strategic leadership role backed by over a decade of distinguished experience spanning radio broadcasting, talent development, media relations and corporate brand communications. An alumnus of Presbyterian Boys’ Senior High School (PRESEC, Legon) and Pentecost University College, where he obtained a BA in Communications, PR & Advertising, he holds a Master of Science in Brands and Communications Management from the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA). Over the past ten years, he has established himself as a prominent voice on the Ghanaian airwaves through his work with various media houses, including Starr FM. In his capacity as PRO for the 5th Praise Achievement Awards, Mawunya-ko will oversee full-scale public relations operations, strategic press engagements, corporate media partnerships and digital communication campaigns. His office will focus on expanding the global footprint of the awards, structuring high-impact media visibility and managing communications as the event celebrates five years of honouring gospel music excellence across Ghana, Africa and the diaspora. “I am profoundly honoured to step into this role for such a milestone anniversary of the Praise Achievement Awards,” stated Precious Mawunya-ko. “Gospel music in Ghana and across the continent carries extraordinary spiritual and cultural weight. My goal for this 5th edition is to bring strategic structure, elevated visibility, and seamless media coverage that honours the hard work of our gospel creatives and projects their impact onto the global stage.” His appointment comes as preparations intensify for the 5th edition of the Praise Achievement Awards, scheduled for Sunday, 13 December 2026. The event is expected to bring together leading gospel artistes, ministers, media professionals, industry stakeholders and audiences from Ghana, Africa and the diaspora. About Praise Achievement Awards The Praise Achievement Awards is a premier gospel music recognition scheme established to celebrate, honour and promote excellence among gospel music ministers, producers, creatives and key stakeholders across Ghana and the international community.

items.title: Aston Villa officialise l’arrivée d’Ibrahim Mbaye, le PSG empoche 55 M€
items.description: Aston Villa a officialisé, ce mardi, la signature d'Ibrahim Mbaye. L'attaquant sénégalais de 18 ans, formé au PSG après son passage par le FC Versailles 78 en 2018, quitte le club parisien contre environ 55 millions d'euros, selon des informations concordantes de The Athletic. Il s'est engagé sur le long terme avec le club de Birmingham, après avoir passé sa visite médicale samedi. Longtemps annoncé du côté de Liverpool, avec qui il avait trouvé un accord contractuel de cinq ans, Mbaye a finalement rejoint le club d'Unai Emery, la bonne relation entre les présidents Nasser Al-Khelaïfi et Nassef Sawiris ayant facilité les négociations entre les deux clubs. Auteur de ses débuts professionnels dès août 2024, à seulement 16 ans, l'ailier quitte le PSG après 42 matches, quatre buts et quatre passes décisives, mais surtout double vainqueur de la Ligue des champions. International sénégalais à 15 reprises, il avait également disputé la dernière Coupe du monde avec les Lions, inscrivant même un but face à l'équipe de France. Avec cette vente, le PSG poursuit un été record sur le marché des transferts, entre les arrivées et les départs, portant à près de 380 millions d'euros les recettes générées par le club parisien depuis l'ouverture du mercato estival. C.G.D

items.title: Don’t let poor English define your potential – Prisons Service DG to Ghanaians
items.description: The Director-General of the Ghana Prisons Service (GPS), Patience Baffoe-Bonnie, has urged Ghanaians to stop equating success with proficiency in the English language, saying that inability to speak English fluently should not be the yardstick to define a person’s potential. She said people, irrespective of their level of formal education or ability to speak English, had unique talents and capacities that could be developed to make meaningful contributions to society. Mrs Baffoe-Bonnie was delivering the keynote address at the Image of a Woman Conference 2026 held on Saturday in Accra. The event, held on the theme “Empowered to Influence, Equipped to Lead, Created to Impact,” brought together about 200 stakeholders drawn from various sectors of the country to discuss women’s leadership, empowerment, entrepreneurship, mentorship, and social transformation. She observed that in many African societies, people who could not speak English well often felt that opportunities were closed to them, particularly when they found themselves in environments where English proficiency was highly valued. She said individuals needed to understand themselves, identify their strengths and weaknesses, work on their shortcomings, and develop the mindset to overcome failure and criticism. “The difference between those who succeed and those who remain where they are has always been the mindset and the fear that people will tease you and that you’re not good enough,” she said. The Director-General, reflecting on her almost 37 years in the GPS, said influence was often built through small, consistent decisions, and people must not wait for formal titles before making an impact. She encouraged women to take responsibility for their own development and leadership and said they did not require permission to make a difference in the positions they already occupied. Mrs Baffoe-Bonnie said achieving her remarkable feat of being the first woman to rise through the ranks to become Director-General of the Prisons and the second woman to occupy the position demonstrated the importance of perseverance, preparation and faith. She said her ability to navigate challenges in her career reinforced her belief that people should identify their God-given abilities and develop them regardless of the circumstances they faced. Mrs Baffoe-Bonnie suggested that people with practical knowledge and experience should be recognised as authorities in their respective fields. She urged citizens to question systems and institutions that restricted opportunities and become part of efforts to create change. She challenged society to take responsibility for the continued stereotyping of women rather than blaming historical structures alone. “If those who set the boundaries for women are no more there and we continue to promote that kind of conduct, then who are rather those stereotyping?” Mrs Baffoe-Bonnie asked. She said religion could play a role in reinforcing stereotypes and called for greater reflection among religious and community leaders. Prophetess Aku Xornam Adzraku-Kevi, the conference convener, explained that the event was designed to create a platform for broader discussion on issues affecting women. She said her work, over the years, had focused on reproductive health, livelihood empowerment, sexual and gender-based violence, and leadership development for women and girls. Prophetess Adzraku-Kevi, the Executive Director of the Purim African Youth Development Platform (PAYDP), said the conference, inspired by her book, “The Image of a Woman,” had carefully brought together religious leaders, civil society organisations, development partners, government officials, parliamentarians, and other stakeholders to ensure that discussions about women extended beyond the religious space. “We want to talk about issues of women; we want to talk about how we can support the lives of other women so that they can take it to their pulpits, and then there can be greater and broader discussions,” she said. She encouraged Ghanaian women not to allow barriers to prevent them from pursuing leadership and success. “You can make it, you can reach the top. There’s nothing too small for you,” she said. The Convener, also the General Overseer of the Glorious Abundant Ministries International, commended the government for what she described as “improvements in its handling of women’s issues but called for more progress, particularly increased representation of women in Parliament and the eventual election of a woman as president. She expressed appreciation to the conference’s partners, including UNFPA, Forward UK, International Needs, PrimeCert, Adehyeɛ Mma, Glorious Abundant Ministries International, and other supporting organisations for helping to organise the programme. The conference also honoured veteran media personality Madam Rosemary Ardayfio for her contribution to journalism, media excellence, and mentorship.

items.title: G-100: Turaki-led PDP joins opposition move to defeat Tinubu
items.description: The Kabiru Tanimu Turaki-led faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has endorsed the G-100 (a group of 100 opposition stalwarts) driven process of creating an all-opposition front to challenge President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. A statement on Tuesday by the faction’s National Publicity Secretary, Ini Ememobong, said the decision was informed by the “wailings of Nigerians groaning under the repressive Bola Tinubu APC-led Federal Government,” and the need to cooperate with other credible political forces to unseat the incumbent at the federal level. It quoted the faction’s National Chairman, Turaki, as saying, “Our participation is anchored on the promise that the process will be hinged on the philosophical underpinnings of transparency, equality, data-driven decisions and egalitarianism. Any result birthed by a process midwifed by these virtues will certainly offer Nigerians a credible leadership capable of alleviating the skyrocketing poverty and rising insecurity in the country.” Ememobong added, “This new move aligns with our earlier stated disposition of working with like-minded political parties and organisations desirous of salvaging the country from the many vices orchestrated by the ruling APC. “Our participation at the first meeting of the G-100 on 31st August, 2026 is a further indication of our preparedness to contribute our quota in the quest for an all-opposition platform that will take power from the incumbent and rebuild Nigeria for the good of all Nigerians.” The post G-100: Turaki-led PDP joins opposition move to defeat Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GRIDCo’s operating profit plunges 89% despite net profit surge in 2025
items.description: The Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo) recorded a sharp decline in its core financial performance in 2025, with operating profit falling by 89.45 per cent despite an increase in net profit. According to the 2025 State Ownership Report by the State Interests and Governance Authority (SIGA), GRIDCo’s operating profit dropped from GH¢955.19 million in 2024 to GH¢100.82 million in 2025. The decline caused the company’s operating profit margin to fall from 26.65 per cent to 3.65 per cent over the period. “Between FY2024 and FY2025, GRIDCo’s financial performance was mixed, with a sharp decline in core operating profitability more than offset by an extraordinary rise in finance income,” the report stated. GRIDCo’s total revenue remained broadly unchanged at GH¢3.60 billion, while operating revenue increased marginally by 1.06 per cent, from GH¢2.66 billion in 2024 to GH¢2.69 billion in 2025. However, the company generated significantly less operating profit from the revenue recorded during the year. Its cost-recovery ratio also declined slightly from 101.92 per cent to 101.24 per cent, indicating that operating revenue continued to exceed operating costs, but by a narrower margin. Despite the deterioration in its core operations, GRIDCo’s net profit increased by 89.02 per cent, from GH¢309.23 million in 2024 to GH¢584.46 million in 2025. SIGA attributed the profit growth mainly to a sharp increase in finance income rather than an improvement in the company’s principal electricity transmission operations. Finance income rose from GH¢16.36 million in 2024 to GH¢838.51 million in 2025. “Net profit nonetheless increased by 89.02 per cent, from GH¢309.23 million to GH¢584.46 million, primarily driven by an extraordinary rise in finance income and other income,” the report said. The additional income lifted GRIDCo’s net profit margin from 8.59 per cent to 17.42 per cent. Return on equity also increased from 2.07 per cent to 5.31 per cent, while return on assets rose from 0.71 per cent to 3.77 per cent. Beyond the decline in operating profit, GRIDCo’s balance sheet contracted substantially during the year. Total assets fell by about 21 per cent, from GH¢27.70 billion in 2024 to GH¢21.97 billion in 2025. Total equity also declined by 26.36 per cent, from GH¢14.96 billion to GH¢11.01 billion. The reduction was attributed mainly to a revaluation loss on property, plant and equipment. “For FY2025, GRIDCo’s capital structure weakened despite a significant reduction in borrowings,” SIGA stated. The fall in equity increased the company’s debt-to-assets ratio from 0.46 to 0.49, while its equity multiplier rose from 1.85 to 2.00, signalling slightly higher financial leverage. GRIDCo nevertheless reduced its interest-bearing liabilities by 34.97 per cent, from GH¢2.86 billion in 2024 to GH¢1.86 billion in 2025. Total debt and liabilities also declined from GH¢12.74 billion to GH¢10.96 billion. However, the company’s interest-coverage ratio fell from 1.23 times to 0.92 times, meaning its operating profit was no longer sufficient to cover its finance costs fully. “The interest coverage ratio moved from 1.23 to 0.92 times, meaning operating profit (EBIT) no longer fully covers finance costs,” the report warned. GRIDCo also experienced a substantial decline in cash generated from its operations. Net operating cash flow fell by about 58 per cent, from GH¢1.45 billion in 2024 to GH¢616.05 million in 2025. SIGA said the decline in operating cash-flow indicators demonstrated a “substantial weakening in operating cash generation” during the year. Cash and cash equivalents, however, increased by 3.71 per cent, from GH¢965.74 million to GH¢1.00 billion, while the company’s current ratio showed a modest improvement. GRIDCo is wholly owned by the government and is responsible for operating Ghana’s national electricity transmission system, including building and maintaining transmission lines and substations.

items.title: IGP summons Volta Police Commander over alleged extortion of traders on Aflao–Accra route
items.description: The Inspector-General of Police (IGP) has summoned the Volta Regional Police Commander following concerns over alleged harassment, intimidation, unnecessary delays, and extortion of local traders by some police personnel along the Aflao–Accra main route. Following the development, the Regional Commander has consequently summoned all Divisional and District Commanders to a meeting on Wednesday, September 2, 2026, to deliberate on the matter and take appropriate measures. The concerns follow a viral video posted on social media alleging that some police personnel at Tokor Barrier, Ativuta toll booth, Weta–Afiadenyigba junction barrier and other locations towards Sogakope demand receipts for goods being transported by local traders and allegedly extort monies from those unable to produce them. The Joint Association of Port Transport Unions (JAPTU) has also appealed to senior police officers to intervene, stressing that their concern is not the number of checkpoints but rather the alleged unnecessary delays, intimidation, and extortion of traders. “The allegations are of concern as Ghana, through institutions including the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) and Ghana Shippers’ Authority (GSA), is making efforts to promote its ports and transit corridors to neighbouring countries to boost trade and economic growth,” a statement issued by the Ghana Police Service said. It said personnel deployed to the affected locations had been cautioned against misconduct. “An inspection team is also being constituted to identify and investigate personnel involved in such acts, with appropriate disciplinary measures to be taken where allegations are substantiated,” it said.

items.title: Welcome to Girlie-Pop Woodstock
items.description: Early Saturday afternoon at the Daisy Chain Fields festival, in Irvine, California, the 25-year-old singer Eli twirled in a tank top emblazoned with a cartoon guitar while singing songs whose plasticky violins recalled the kind of music played on the Disney Channel in 2004. Dancers waved poles with dresses attached to them as if they were flags. She took out her phone, whose case was shaped like a cute bear, and read some thoughts she’d jotted down. “This journal entry is to show you my fundamental belief that we must redistribute wealth,” she said. “We must love our neighbors no matter what they believe or don’t. We must unite with each other and radicalize. Eat the identity politics that deceive and divide us all, as well as”—here she broke into a ragged moan—“eating the rich!” Eli is a campy artist of questionable earnestness, but her statement was in line with the mood of Daisy Chain—a place where girlish aesthetics that are so often seen as frivolous could accompany calls for revolution. Organized by the 23-year-old pop star Olivia Rodrigo, the inaugural edition of the festival featured an all-female lineup and raised $20 million—half of which was donated by Melinda French Gates—for an array of women’s-rights organizations, including Planned Parenthood and the National Domestic Workers Alliance. Even as a brutal heat wave threatened to smother the energy, the fest felt like a cheerful coming-out party—an announcement of the political commitments of a generation of mainstream artists more famous for singing about the self than about society. Rodrigo patterned Daisy Chain off of Lilith Fair, the best-selling female-fronted touring festival that ran from 1997 to 1999, but the two events are a study in contrasts. Lilith’s co-founder Sarah McLachlan wanted to prove the viability of female musicians at a time when, she told the LA Times , radio programmers were reluctant to play two of them back-to-back. The lineup reflected a boom in singer-songwriters—Tracy Chapman, Jewel, Paula Cole, Indigo Girls—whose socially conscientious songs harkened back to the spirit of Woodstock (an obvious influence on the flower-powery Daisy Chain as well). Lilith’s aesthetics were earthen and earnest—a celebration of an ideal of strong, serious womanhood, much to the perturbation of late-night comics who cracked jokes about Cole’s armpit hair. Today, women aren’t so marginal to the record industry; in fact, it can sometimes seem like Taylor Swift and her disciples are the record industry. But with power has come an inversion in content and style. The dominant female musical archetype of the 2020s isn’t the diva or the chanteuse—it’s the girlie , a term that conveys knowing immaturity and kitsch femininity. Girlies write songs about kinky sex while calling themselves princesses (as does the Daisy Chain singer Chappell Roan), or rap tough and fast while slathered in Barbie-pink body paint (as Doechii did on Saturday). The word is gendered, but it refers to a disposition, and thus can encompass gay guys and even those shy and sweet straight men known as babygirls . Daisy Chain was for the girlies. Irvine’s Great Park was turned into a Lewis Carroll wonderland pocked with floral arrangements that seemed like crayon drawings come to life. Young kids ran around in tiaras while adults blended frilliness and adolescent-alternative stylings: blond locks with streaks of slime green, or the undying rebel-girl look of baby-doll dresses and Doc Martens. I wondered whether the commitment to daintiness explained even the dearth of shade at the fest; the tasseled umbrellas dotting the grounds were totally adorable and terribly unmatched to an El Niño August. Girlie nation has arisen slowly, over decades. As my colleague Sophie Gilbert reported in her book Girl on Girl , Lilith Fair’s vision of female artistry was sidelined as record labels and radio stations began to favor smiling, pliable teenagers such as Britney Spears. Twenty-first-century youths grew up with former Mouseketeers serving as aspirational figures—and, eventually, as cautionary tales about giving up one’s agency for fame. Following in the example of Swift, who built on her teen-princess image with her own formidable songwriting, the new female guard arose. Some, like Rodrigo and Sabrina Carpenter, were trained by Disney; others, like Billie Eilish and Rachel Chinouriri (an ascendent U.K. singer and a Daisy Chain booking), got their start at home, posting music online. All of them project control with every slickly witty, emotionally frank, personally revealing hit they write. What they haven’t projected much of, in their songs, at least, is the political edge of the Lilith crowd. Jewel broke out with an album whose title song made a shockingly frontal attack on bigotry (“You say he’s a faggot; does he make you sick to your stomach?”). But today’s young stars mostly just side-eye society’s problems in lyrical tales of hookups, breakups, and anxiety. When Roan calls for a “Femininomenon” (one song title), she’s implicitly calling for feminist change, but she’s explicitly calling just for more girls to ditch their dudes. It’s not that Gen Z has nothing to say—many of these singers will readily riff about ICE and Gaza on their Instagram and in public comments. Rodrigo even delivered an onstage F.U. to the Supreme Court after the fall of national abortion rights, in 2022. But when it comes to their music, they prefer to focus mostly on the personal. Perhaps that’s because their milieu is the isolation and intimacy of the smartphone-enabled bedroom, not the social jungle of rock clubs and coffee shops. Maybe it’s because they watched progressive pop of the mid-2010s cheer Hillary Clinton’s failed presidential campaign and then spin itself into an even more didactic fervor during Donald Trump’s first term. On some level, girliehood may be a defensive posture amid conservative cultural backlash: a way to speak and shout and command lots of influence without being seen as threatening. Indeed, Daisy Chain inevitably raised the question of how potent mere cultural visibility can be. Lines of people snaked through the grounds throughout the day—some for art installations by female artists, and many for immersive brand activations, including a pink, larger-than-life Taco Bell Baja Blast that had been scrawled on with diary-cursive font. The festival was a co-production of the convicted monopoly Live Nation and felt, in execution, like a re-skinned version of moneymaking glitz fests such as Coachella. Eli’s rallying cry with a side of giggles aside, the fest was not destabilizing power structures—it was part of them. Rodrigo is probably not the person to figure out what true counterculture might mean in this, the most consumerist decade of human history. Still, she’s trying. Daisy Chain’s two stages were festooned with mock buttons, like on a backpack, that advertised the fest’s 10 nonprofit beneficiaries (representatives for which got to speak to the crowds before various sets). This great design decision served whimsical eye candy, evoked a lineage of hippies and women’s libbers, and dispensed useful information. The featured slogans— Bans off our bodies , Reproductive rights are human rights , WOMEN ROCK BETTER —hardly read like safe platitudes in post- Dobbs America, where some conservatives now openly yearn to roll back women’s right to vote . Rodrigo is also at last tackling overt protest music. Shortly before the festival, she released a coolly seething post-punk single called “Serena Joy,” named for a character in The Handmaid’s Tale . Its exact concerns are a bit hazy: A lyric about gold-painted towers indirectly sneers at Trump, and a mention of bothered “neighbors” could be about ICE deportations or even tariffs on Canada. What’s clear is her overall call to wake up and fight back. I get shivers when she sings, “If you can’t throw a punch / You can learn how to spit.” The fest’s lineup also made a statement by tracing an intergenerational feminist lineage instead of just spotlighting trendy new acts. One invitee was the ’90s rock band Garbage, whose singer, Shirley Manson, made painfully heartfelt speeches about resilience, growing older, and LGBTQ acceptance. Another was the indie band the Breeders, whose cooed harmonies and twisted guitars are the bay-leaf influence on Rodrigo’s tangiest songs. The reggae-inflected alternative singer Santigold—a representative of the 2000s indie landscape—invited members of the crowd onstage for a joyful, if less than impressively skilled, dance contest. The most telling booking was Bikini Kill, the punk band whose riot-grrrl sound flipped clichés about demure young womanhood way back in the early ’90s. The lead singer, Kathleen Hanna, opened with some political scene setting: “This government hates us and wants us dead. They don’t give a shit about anybody’s health care. They don’t care if we’re dying in parking lots of curable illnesses.” Then she got to croaking and gyrating with a ferocity that offered a reminder to the Instagram-generation viewers that playing pretty isn’t the only way to command eyeballs. “This is the most engaged crowd I’ve ever seen in my life,” she said at one point, and a reason was clear: At Bikini Kill’s early shows, she would call for men to make room for girls to come to the front of the crowd, but here, she didn’t need to do that. Read: How indie rock changed the world Still, the festival’s greatest highlights came from gutsy and well-executed performances by young people. The first act of the day, the experimental electronic-pop artist Quiet Light, offered a calm and cooling welcome as she executed slow choreo in a billowing nightie. Later, the blue-haired songwriter Devon Again—a last-minute replacement after the girl group Katseye dropped out—knocked me back with country-tinged electro rock as crunchy as a kettle chip. In a stunt that recalled bros such as Blink-182 and Red Hot Chili Peppers, her band members dropped trou at the start of the set and rocked in their boxers. As the sun fell, Roan took to the stage for a happy-go-lucky display of dominance. Her band, dressed in snazzy ’80s power suits, whipped up simmering disco tension punctuated by Van Halen–style guitar eruptions. Roan, who was styled like a flight attendant from the ’90s sci-fi movie The Fifth Element , also acted all-business: spare with her banter and springy on her feet as she flicked between chatty verses and lung-busting choruses. After that stratospheric spectacle, Rodrigo’s headlining set felt a bit like a wobbly-legged return to Earth. Although she can dig deep and nail the big moments—“The Cure” sounded bottomlessly sad—she often leans too heavily on actorly tics that overplay the considerable personality already inherent in her lyrics. Listening to her sing her stellar recent song “Maggots for Brains,” I had the thought that her songwriting talent, bar for bar, matches almost any of her predecessors’. Just then, some predecessors joined her: first McLachlan, for a festival-shushing rendition of “Building a Mystery” and “Angel,” and then Alanis Morissette, to grin and yowl “Ironic.” The Gen X parents in the crowd, clearly worn down by a day of sticky-hot chaperoning, suddenly came alive. The final song of the night was the most moving one: Rodrigo and Stevie Nicks, another special guest, singing “Landslide.” Their delivery was so careful and crystalline that no one could miss the relevance of the lyrics about generations bound together by time’s forward march. When Nicks sang, “Yes, I’m getting older too,” on her own, with a sad smile, my gut twisted at the thought of the trailblazers we’ve lost lately . But Nicks also conveyed hope—because today’s girls are only at the beginning of what they’ll accomplish.

items.title: What Howard Zinn Got Wrong
items.description: “What would Howard say?” This question, which Dave Zirin reports being “asked repeatedly” while he was working on his new biography of Howard Zinn , underscores how unusual a figure his subject cut in contemporary American life. Most historians live and die in relative obscurity. But 16 years after Zinn’s death, many people still look to him, not just as a scholar but as a kind of sage. Zinn first became famous—and, in some circles, infamous—after the 1980 publication of his best-selling work A People’s History of the United States . The book advanced an ambitious and unrepentantly radical reimagining of the nation’s past. Zinn rejected the conventional organization of history around “the point of view of governments, conquerors, diplomats, leaders” and declared, “I prefer to try to tell the story of the discovery of America from the viewpoint of the Arawaks, of the Constitution from the standpoint of the slaves, of Andrew Jackson as seen by the Cherokees.” What emerged was a new grand narrative, one that promised to reveal what mainstream history had long concealed and to offer a new moral framework for the past. In Zinn’s telling, the powerful were almost always up to no good, and ordinary people were the heroes of the American story. They courageously built movements for justice and sometimes even won, though it never took long for the oppressors to regroup. The fight was never over. Unlike most best sellers, A People’s History never stopped selling. Each year during its first three decades in print, it sold more copies than the last. The book’s fans applauded its bottom-up, justice-minded approach to history, while its detractors dismissed it as a leftist morality play masquerading as a story about the past. No one could doubt that it changed the conversation about American history, not to mention the trajectory of Zinn’s life. By the time he died in 2010, he was an archvillain for the right and a secular saint for the left. Zirin’s fast-paced biography, The People’s Historian , is an answer to the most interesting version of “What would Howard say?” One hardly needs to squint to imagine what Zinn would have thought of the current regime in Washington, and readers curious only about that can put this book down after page 4, where Zirin declares, “Fascist movements taking orders from billionaire insurrectionists were the kinds of struggles that Howard Zinn demonstrated a willingness to fight and, if necessary, die to oppose.” But Zirin himself is after something more. He knew Zinn personally and collaborated with him on projects; he admires him deeply. Zirin believes we need more than Zinn’s opinions today; he argues that we need the deeper wisdom that emanates from his life and work. Zinn’s many gifts developed in the course of what was, by any estimation, a remarkable journey. He was born in 1922 to working-class Jewish immigrants in Brooklyn. In his early 20s he rushed to enlist in the fight against fascism, serving in the Air Forces during World War II. He would long regret his short tenure as a bombardier who dropped artillery shells on behalf of a compromised colonial power—as he would later come to see the United States—from such heights that he could not be sure where exactly they landed. Zinn’s willingness to admit he was gravely wrong is part of what Zirin loves about him. The people’s historian was a radical, but he was also a “happy warrior” who believed that people could change, and so could societies. [ Read: The new history wars ] As a participant in the civil-rights and anti-war movements, Zinn witnessed such transformations firsthand. He organized alongside his students at Spelman College as well as with famous activists, including Ella Baker and Daniel Berrigan . Together, in the 1960s and ’70s, they fought to change a country whose past and present were steeped in violence and white supremacy. The going was never easy, because, as Zirin tells it—very much in Zinnian fashion—they bumped up against so many villains in power. Sometimes it was the director of the FBI; other times, a reactionary university administrator. But the people could be powerful too. Any given campaign might be stymied, but the march went on. However dreary the news, the hope persisted for a better day. Zirin argues convincingly that Zinn’s life story vindicates one of his deepest convictions: that ordinary people and “small acts” can change the world. Zinn was right about this, and Zirin concludes the book with a quote from him that draws out the optimistic implications of his faith in bottom-up movements: “We have been surprised before in history. We can be surprised again. Indeed, we can do the surprising.” This is a compelling message for the current moment—and any other. Yet one can agree with Zinn on the power of the people to make change and still wonder whether recent history has revealed the limits of his wisdom. “Was he wrong to have faith in the people?” Zirin relates that some of Zinn’s devotees—“those politically raised on his ideas”—have asked him this question, in addition to the one about what he might say in any given situation. Zirin takes up the second query but answers it far less satisfactorily than the first. He acknowledges that “in 2024, 77 million voters checked the box for an authoritarian to take power once again,” and moreover that Trump “won masses of white working-class people and, according to political pundits, a not-insignificant number of Black and Latino men.” But Zirin does not wrestle with the meaning of these developments. Rather, he waves them away with invocations of the “tech oligarchs” and “autocrats” who are driving “our global descent into authoritarianism.” This is an homage in a way, a vintage Zinn move—evading tough questions about who “the people” are and what they really want. A People’s History of the United States appeared the same year Ronald Reagan was first elected president. In later editions of the book, Zinn would cast Reagan—like Jimmy Carter before him and George H. W. Bush after—as a creature of “the Establishment,” elected by a majority of voters but by a minority of the voting population and, hence, hardly the people’s choice. Zinn wrote something similar in 2003 amid the travails of the early War on Terror: “I wake up in the morning, read the newspaper, and feel that we are an occupied country, that some alien group has taken over.” The following year, of course, George W. Bush won the popular vote. [ Read: What if our ancestors didn’t feel anything like we do? ] Zinn was hardly the only academic to be thrown by this turn of events. The 2004 election left no doubt that the Reagan Revolution had been more than a blip; in its aftermath, American historians redoubled their efforts to understand the sources of the right’s surprising resurgence. What they have uncovered in the past two decades flies in the face of a central tenet of Zinnian orthodoxy. The sustained success of the modern conservative movement cannot be explained away as the outcome of establishment machinations or a top-down takeover. Its energy and vitality came in no small part from the grassroots: from stay-at-home moms and car mechanics, from the suburbs and the Sun Belt, from evangelicals and Catholics and more. The revival of the Republican Party’s national fortunes at various moments, going all the way back to Richard Nixon, confirms Zinn’s faith in the power of bottom-up movements, even as it confounds his almost mythic sense of “the people” as inevitably on the right side of history (that is, the left side of the political spectrum). And if ordinary folks are more complicated than Zinn and Zirin recognize, perhaps those who wield power can be too. What made the right’s political comeback so surprising, after all, was that in the mid-1960s the liberal-left coalition was winning not only in the streets but also on Capitol Hill. In those years, progressives leveraged grassroots energy into breakthrough policy change. The leaders of major civic and political institutions were rarely out in front of progressive activists, but at least some of them chose to pull levers that made the United States more equal and just. The Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 passed with sweeping bipartisan majorities. After an outrageous assault by law enforcement on peaceful demonstrators in Selma, Alabama, President Lyndon B. Johnson memorably proclaimed —before a joint session of Congress, Cabinet officers, Supreme Court justices, and more than 70 million Americans watching on television—that “it is not just Negroes, but really it is all of us, who must overcome the crippling legacy of bigotry and injustice. And—we—shall—overcome.” His invocation of a beloved civil-rights anthem brought a tear to Martin Luther King Jr.’s eye. None of this impressed Zinn. In A People’s History , he framed both the speech and the landmark civil-rights legislation of the 1960s as “concessions.” Then and now, such unrelenting suspicion springs from genuine patterns of institutional failure and betrayal. Villains are, alas, not just a figment of our collective imagination. And yet, in 2026, with the Democrats on the outside of power looking in, progressives might nevertheless ask whether the Zinnian propensity to demonize anyone and everyone wielding authority has served their cause well. Dismissing landmark legislation as mere concessions can miss the fact that there is no path forward from righteous protest to lasting change that does not run through better—if imperfect—public policy. However “exhilarating” Zinn’s counternarrative can be, it may have encouraged millions of well-meaning readers to be skeptical of the possibility that any good could come through the slow, messy institutional work that is central to pluralistic democracy. Coincidental or not, this much is true: During the same period when Zinn’s influence was rising meteorically on the left, the right became much more adept at channeling populist enthusiasm into deliberate campaigns to reshape the major institutions of American life. “I wanted to change the world, and I thought history might be helpful,” Zinn liked to say, lightheartedly. His biographer is right to argue that Zinn, an ordinary person, did change the world—though perhaps he didn’t do it only in the ways that either of them hoped he would.

items.title: Amin Adam: Gold programme lost money despite 62.9% rise in prices
items.description: Former Finance Minister, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, says Ghana’s gold purchase programme failed to deliver the expected financial benefits despite a significant rise in international gold prices in 2025. The Karaga MP said gold prices increased by 62.9 per cent during the year, moving from an average of US$2,395 per ounce to US$3,441. Speaking at a press conference on Tuesday, September 1, he described the performance as one of the strongest years for gold in decades, yet said Ghana’s programme continued to incur substantial losses. “This was not the market’s fault,” Dr Amin Adam said. According to him, three major costs were built into every transaction: exchange-rate differences, discounts to foreign buyers and handling fees. He said the Bank of Ghana advanced cedis at the official interbank rate while GoldBod paid miners at higher rates available through forex bureaus. “The Bank advanced cedis at the official interbank rate while GoldBod paid miners at the higher rate available at forex bureaus. The Bank absorbed that gap on every purchase,” he said. Dr Amin Adam also cited the discount given to foreign buyers, saying Ghana sold gold in October 2025 at US$3,919 an ounce compared with a world average of US$4,054. He said the discount represented a significant cost to the country. “A discount to foreign buyers… is money that never reached Ghana,” he said. He further criticised the 0.5 per cent service fee and 0.258 per cent assay fee charged on the full value of transactions.

items.title: Secteur portuaire : l’APN valide son rapport 2025 et pose les jalons de la compétitivité
items.description: © DR Siégeant le 27 août 2026 pour sa 93e session, le Conseil d'administration de l'Autorité Portuaire Nationale a examiné et adopté le rapport sur l'état du secteur portuaire national au titre de l'exercice 2025, présenté par le DG Willie Tsanga Mba. Cap sur la performance portuaire. L'Autorité Portuaire Nationale (APN) a tenu jeudi 27 août 2026, dans sa salle du Conseil d'administration, sa 93e session consacrée au bilan du secteur portuaire national. Les travaux ont été présidés par M. Abdoul Nassir, Président de séance du Conseil d'administration. Le rapport de référence a été présenté par le Directeur général, M. Willie Tsanga Mba, assisté de Mme Ayuketah Pamela, Directrice générale adjointe. Document stratégique, ce rapport dresse un état des lieux exhaustif des performances des différentes places portuaires camerounaises et met en exergue les évolutions significatives enregistrées en 2025. Il permet d'appréhender la dynamique du secteur et d'identifier les défis persistants, à l'heure où les infrastructures portuaires restent un maillon vital de l'économie, assurant l'essentiel des échanges avec l'extérieur. Au-delà du bilan, l'examen offre aux administrateurs une meilleure visibilité sur les perspectives à moyen terme et les leviers de compétitivité. Adopté au terme des travaux, ce rapport s'impose comme outil de référence pour faire des ports camerounais des destinations plus dynamiques, compétitives, sûres et durables. Cet article Secteur portuaire : l'APN valide son rapport 2025 et pose les jalons de la compétitivité est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Simandou et réforme administrative : «si nous ne nous organisons pas, on risque de rater une opportunité rare», prévient Bah Oury
items.description: Alors que le projet minier de Simandou est présenté comme l’un des principaux leviers du développement socio-économique de la Guinée sous le régime de Mamadi Doumbouya, la capacité de l’administration publique à accompagner efficacement sa mise en œuvre préoccupe au plus haut sommet de l’État. Lors d’une rencontre avec les cadres de la haute administration publique, consacrée notamment à la performance et à l’organisation institutionnelle, le Premier ministre, chef du gouvernement, Amadou Oury Bah, a tiré la sonnette d’alarme sur les défis auxquels l’appareil d’État doit faire face pour permettre à la Guinée de tirer pleinement profit des retombées de Simandou. Dans une intervention relayée par les canaux officiels de la Primature, le chef du gouvernement a notamment insisté sur la nécessité pour l’administration de se préparer à la hauteur des enjeux liés à ce projet stratégique. « La véritable question est : est-ce que nous avons l’administration et la méthodologie nécessaires pour assurer le suivi et la mise en œuvre de manière efficace, pour que le programme Simandou puisse se réaliser conformément aux instructions et à la vision du président de la République ? », s’est-il interrogé. Poursuivant son analyse, Bah Oury a souligné le rôle déterminant de la haute administration dans la traduction des orientations stratégiques du gouvernement en actions concrètes. « Des structures ont été pensées, mais comme vous le savez, l’administration, surtout la haute administration, doit impérativement être suffisamment prête pour accompagner la mise en œuvre. Et la mise en œuvre passe principalement à travers les structures ministérielles et les autres structures qui sont là pour appuyer les structures ministérielles, afin d’assurer l’efficacité et l’opérationnalisation de tous les projets », a-t-il expliqué. Le Premier ministre a également insisté sur les importantes retombées financières attendues de l’exploitation de Simandou, tout en mettant en garde contre le risque de laisser passer une occasion historique faute d’une organisation administrative adaptée. « On a dit qu’il y aura beaucoup de revenus pour la Guinée, mais très souvent, si nous ne nous organisons pas en conséquence, on risque d’avoir une opportunité rare et de ne pas pouvoir l’exploiter avec efficience pour la transformation de notre pays », a averti Bah Oury. Pour lui, la réussite de cette ambition passe nécessairement par une profonde évolution des pratiques administratives et managériales. « C’est la raison pour laquelle il faut revoir nos méthodes, revoir notre style de management pour correspondre à ce qu’on attend de nous », a-t-il martelé. Cette sortie du chef du gouvernement intervient dans le cadre des efforts engagés par les autorités pour renforcer la performance de l’administration publique et l’adapter aux exigences des grands projets structurants, notamment le programme Simandou. À travers cet appel à une meilleure organisation, à davantage d’efficacité et à une culture du résultat, le gouvernement entend ainsi préparer l’appareil d’État à gérer les importantes ressources attendues de ce projet et à les convertir en investissements capables d’accélérer la transformation économique et sociale du pays.

items.title: Plus de 5 000 décès liés à la chaleur en Espagne, 0 en Tunisie !
items.description: L’Espagne a annoncé un lourd bilan de décès causés par la chaleur entre le 1 er juin et le 31 août 2026. C’est un record pour cette période depuis que l’Institut de santé Carlos III a commencé à collecter ces données en 2015. En Tunisie, le ministère de la Santé refuse toujours de communiquer sur le nombre de décès causés par la canicule sévissant depuis plusieurs semaines dans le pays, et ce, malgré les interpellations à ce propos de la part des professionnels de la santé opérant dans les hôpitaux publics. En Espagne, la chaleur a causé la mort de 2 025 personnes en juin, 937 en juillet et 2 149 en août, soit un total de 5 111 décès, selon les données de l’institut citées par l’AFP. Le précédent record pour ces trois mois datait de 2022, année où 4 652 décès liés à la chaleur avaient été enregistrés. Ces estimations reposent sur le système «MoMo» (surveillance de la mortalité), qui recense quotidiennement les décès en Espagne et calcule l’écart entre le nombre de décès réels et celui des décès attendus, sur la base de données historiques. Le pays devrait connaître une nouvelle hausse des températures dans les prochains jours, alors que celles-ci étaient «inférieures aux normales saisonnières dans plusieurs régions ces derniers jours» , selon l’agence météorologique nationale ; cette dernière a également averti que les températures pourraient dépasser les normales de quelque 10 degrés Celsius au cours du mois de septembre. Les températures en Tunisie au cours des prochains jours seront tout aussi élevées et il est fort à parier, étant donné le manque de médecins, de personnel soignant, d’équipements et même de médicaments dans nos hôpitaux publics, que le nombre de morts causées par la canicule va continuer à augmenter. Est-ce que le ministère de la Santé va se résigner enfin à informer le public sur les dégâts causés par la canicule sur la santé publique, ou va-t-il poursuivre dans sa politique de déni qui consiste à n’annoncer que les bonnes nouvelles, si chère au ministre Mustapha Ferjani ? I. B. items.title: Aston Villa sign Senegal winger Mbaye from PSG
items.description: Aston Villa signed Senegal winger Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain in a deal worth a reported £47 million ($63 million) on Tuesday. Mbaye played 31 times in all competitions for PSG last season as the French club won the Champions League and the Ligue 1 title. The 18-year-old also appeared four times for Senegal at the recent World Cup, netting against France to become the youngest African player to score in the men’s tournament. He has been capped 15 times by Senegal since making his PSG debut aged 16. “Aston Villa is delighted to announce the signing of Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain,” the club said in a statement. “The Senegal international, a bright and exciting young prospect who scored for his country at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, joins on a permanent transfer.” France-born Mbaye is the latest new recruit for Villa after a close-season of upheaval at the Premier League club. Since winning the Europa League last season to end their 30-year trophy drought, Villa have sold Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ollie Watkins, Lucas Digne, Emiliano Martinez and Ezri Konsa. Villa boss Unai Emery has brought in Alejandro Garnacho, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Johan Manzambi, Zion Suzuki, Joao Gomes, Leon Goretzka, Matteo Ruggeri and Nicolas Jackson. AFP The post Aston Villa sign Senegal winger Mbaye from PSG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Amin Adam challenges GoldBod’s GH¢5.45bn surplus
items.description: Karaga Member of Parliament and former Finance Minister, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, has challenged GoldBod’s reported GH¢5.45 billion surplus for 2025, arguing that the figure does not accurately reflect the organisation’s trading performance. Dr Amin Adam said GH¢4.54 billion, representing 81.7 per cent of the reported surplus, was a government capital injection credited to GoldBod’s books on December 30, 2025, just a day before the financial year ended. Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, September 1, he said the money was described in GoldBod’s accounts as revolving trade capital and should therefore not be presented as revenue. “Standard public sector and international accounting rules treat money put in by an owner as capital, not revenue, and GoldBod’s own statements describe it as revolving trade capital,” he said. Dr Amin Adam said GoldBod’s treatment of the money raised questions about the credibility of its reported surplus. “It cannot be capital when that is convenient and revenue when there is something to celebrate,” he stated. He further said that of the remaining GH¢909.9 million, about GH¢827 million was fee income, mostly service charges paid to GoldBod by the Bank of Ghana for the same gold purchase operations. “Almost all of GoldBod’s real income was therefore a commission charged on a programme that lost the country GH¢22 billion,” he said. Dr Amin Adam questioned how GoldBod could report a surplus while the institution providing the funds recorded a major loss. “How does a gold buying operator record a surplus while the institution whose funds it is using records a loss?” he asked. He is calling for GoldBod’s 2025 accounts to be restated to remove the GH¢4.54 billion capital injection from revenue.

En cette fin du mois d’août, elle effectue un road trip en Algérie et partage de belles vidéos de son escapade sur Instagram, soulignant l’accueil chaleureux des Algériens et la beauté des sites visités. Road trip en Algérie… que du bonheur ! écrit la députée. Zahia Hamdane subjuguée par la beauté de Tlemcen Direction l’ouest de l’Algérie avec Tlemcen, comme première étape. Connue comme ‘la perle du Maghreb’, cette ville a subjugué la députée franco-algérienne qui partage ses impressions : « Tlemcen, une ville magnifique, riche d’une histoire qui traverse les siècles et d’un patrimoine qui ne demande qu’à être découvert ». Road trip en Algérie… que du bonheur ! Première étape : Tlemcen, une ville magnifique, riche d’une histoire qui traverse les siècles et d’un patrimoine qui ne demande qu’à être découvert. Entre les impressionnantes grottes de Béni Add, les vestiges majestueux de Mansourah… pic.twitter.com/iHdyhR4Miv — Zahia Hamdane (@ZahiaHamdane) August 31, 2026 Balades, repas partagés en famille, dégustations de saveurs locales, visites de sites historiques, découverte du patrimoine millénaire de l’ancienne Pomaria… dans une ambiance joyeuse et conviviale. La députée savoure son voyage et immortalise ces moments uniques par des vidéos diffusées sur la chanson ‘Zina’ de Raina Rai. Stalactites et stalagmites des grottes de Béni-Add Zahia Hamdane a effectué une virée enchanteresse dans les grottes de Béni-Add, situées dans le parc national de Tlemcen, sur les hauteurs de la commune d’Aïn Fezza, à une vingtaine de kilomètres environ du centre-ville de Tlemcen. Une grotte âgée d’environ 65 000 ans, qui force l’admiration. Sur Instagram, elle évoque l’hospitalité légendaire des Algériens. « L’accueil chaleureux, bienveillant et attentionné des personnes rencontrées. Une générosité qui donne au séjour une saveur toute particulière », témoigne-t-elle. Cap sur Oran La parlementaire annonce poursuivre son escapade dans la ville d’Oran « Et l’aventure continue, avec une nouvelle étape qui nous attend à Oran » En partageant les temps forts de son voyage en Algérie, Zahia Hamdane, la députée franco-algérienne de 61 ans, met en lumière les richesses de notre pays et contribue, telle une ambassadrice, à promouvoir la destination Algérie. Financial challenges remain major concern for Ghana’s power sector – Electrical engineer
items.description: A member of the Ghana Institution of Engineering, electrical engineer Hesford Quaye-Larbi, has identified financial weakness as a major challenge confronting Ghana’s power sector, attributing it partly to persistent electricity losses. According to him, distribution companies are struggling to recover revenue from a significant portion of the electricity supplied to consumers because of technical and commercial losses within the distribution system. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Tuesday, September 1, Mr Quaye-Larbi said current system losses stood at about 27%. “As we speak, the loss is about 27%,” he stated. He explained that when distribution companies receive electricity for sale but lose a significant portion of it before revenue can be recovered, their ability to meet financial obligations is weakened. Using a simple illustration, Mr Quaye-Larbi said if a company received 100 units of electricity but lost 27 units, it could only generate revenue from the remaining 73 units. “So it means you haven’t made a profit. It losses,” he said. He said the revenue shortfall creates a wider financial burden across the power sector, as distribution companies are still required to meet payment obligations to independent power producers and other electricity suppliers. The financial difficulties could also affect government revenue, he added, as financially weak state-owned institutions may struggle to meet their tax obligations. Mr Quaye-Larbi therefore called for greater focus on reducing electricity losses and improving revenue collection as part of efforts to restore financial stability to the sector. He argued that reducing the current level of losses could generate significant additional resources for the sector without necessarily relying immediately on higher electricity tariffs. “The 27%, if we’re able to collect it, I can’t figure out the total amount. It’s a prevalent amount. But it will do a lot,” he said. He also called for investment in transmission and distribution infrastructure to reduce technical losses and improve the efficiency of electricity delivery.

items.title: Messi legacy will ‘live forever’, says Beckham
items.description: David Beckham said Lionel Messi’s “legacy will live forever” after the Argentina legend announced his retirement from international football. Messi on Monday revealed he had called time on his remarkable career with Argentina after 207 caps and 125 goals. The 39-year-old won the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and his last game for his country was Argentina’s World Cup final defeat against Spain in July. Messi’s brilliance for Argentina and Barcelona made him one of the world’s greatest ever players. Former England captain Beckham has had a close-up view of Messi’s career as an opponent and now as co-owner of the forward’s current side Inter Miami. “This is the moment we get to look back on and realise how grateful we were to witness the greatness of a young kid with a dream,” Beckham wrote on Instagram on Tuesday. “Leo, you have been a credit to yourself, your family, your friends and your country. Leading by example and creating inspiration for millions of children not just in Argentina but around the whole world. “Leo, you delivered the greatest gift to your country and, for that, your legacy will live forever. Congratulations on all you achieved for Argentina.” The post Messi legacy will ‘live forever’, says Beckham appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nayef Aguerd devrait finalement rester à l’OM
items.description: Nayef Aguerd se dirige vers une poursuite de son aventure avec l’Olympique de Marseille, après l’échec des négociations pour un départ vers la Real Sociedad. Le défenseur central figure désormais parmi les joueurs que le club phocéen souhaite conserver. Le Marocain faisait partie des éléments susceptibles de quitter Marseille durant ce mercato estival. Son nom avait notamment été associé à la Real Sociedad, mais les discussions entre les différentes parties n’ont pas abouti à un accord définitif, laissant désormais envisager son maintien dans l’effectif marseillais. D’après des informations rapportées par la presse française, la direction de l’OM aurait décidé de conserver Aguerd, aux côtés d’Igor Paixão, Quentin Timber et Emerson, sauf changement de dernière minute avant la fermeture du mercato. Cette décision intervient alors que les mouvements du club en fin de mercato étaient notamment conditionnés à certains départs. Après plusieurs opérations qui n’ont finalement pas abouti, les plans de Marseille auraient évolué, réduisant les possibilités de voir Aguerd quitter le club. L’entraîneur marseillais Bruno Genesio avait d’ailleurs expliqué après la défaite face à Monaco (2-0) que le club ne prévoyait pas de recrue supplémentaire, précisant qu’un éventuel mouvement dépendrait d’abord de départs. Malgré l’intérêt manifesté par plusieurs clubs, la situation d’Aguerd est donc restée incertaine jusqu’aux dernières heures du marché. Son expérience internationale et son importance dans le secteur défensif pourraient finalement convaincre l’OM de miser sur sa continuité. L’échec de son transfert à la Real Sociedad met ainsi fin, pour l’heure, à la perspective d’une nouvelle aventure en Liga. Sauf rebondissement de dernière minute, Aguerd devrait poursuivre la saison sous les couleurs marseillaises. Le défenseur marocain est sous contrat avec l’Olympique de Marseille jusqu’à l’été 2030. The post Nayef Aguerd devrait finalement rester à l’OM appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: RDC : le nombre d’infections confirmées d’Ebola dépasse les 6000 cas
items.description: Le dernier rapport sur la situation epidemiologique des autorites sanitaires de la Republique democratique du Congo (RDC), publie le 31 août par l'Agence congolaise de presse (ACP), a fait etat de 6 041 cas confirmes d'Ebola dans les six provinces affectees par la maladie, avec un bilan de 2 911 deces. La meme source a fait savoir que le nombre de guerisons avait progresse a 1 366 personnes, avec 619 patients traites dans les etablissements de sante. a ce jour, le taux de letalite de la souche Bundibugyo du virus Ebola, pour laquelle il n'existe encore aucun traitement ou vaccin homologue, est de 48,2 %. Les autorites sanitaires congolaises indiquent egalement que le taux de suivi des contacts est de 82,4 %. Cette 17e epidemie du virus Ebola a touche 60 zones de sante reparties sur six provinces de l'est de la RDC, a savoir le Nord-Kivu, le Sud-Kivu, l'Ituri, la Tshopo, le Haut-Uele et le Bas-Uele. La rentree scolaire confirmee sur l'ensemble du territoire congolais et les mesures barrieres preconisees La ministre congolaise de l'education, Raïssa Malu Dinanga, a confirme le 31 août que la rentree scolaire sera effective sur l'ensemble du territoire national, incluant les zones touchees par l'epidemie d'Ebola. Elle a indique dans ce contexte que « des mesures sanitaires renforcees et un dispositif leger d'enseignement a distance pourront etre actives lorsque la situation l'exige, afin d'assurer la continuite des apprentissages », rapporte la presse locale. Pour sa part, l'Institut national de sante publique (INSP) a appele par voie de communique les eleves, les enseignants, les parents et l'ensemble de la communaute educative a observer strictement les mesures barrieres contre la maladie. Des strategies sanitaires ont ete definies par l'INSP lors d'une concertation entre les secteurs de la sante et de l'education, visant a renforcer la prevention, la surveillance et la reponse au sein des etablissements scolaires. a ce propos, le Dr Dieudonne Mwamba Kazadi a declare : « La securite sanitaire de nos enfants et de toute la communaute educative demeure une priorite. Une rentree scolaire reussie est aussi une rentree scolaire protegee ». Les conditions sanitaires ne sont pas encore suffisamment rassurantes pour une rentree scolaire selon la societe civile La decision de generaliser la rentree scolaire meme dans les regions affectees par l'epidemie a souleve des reserves, notamment de la part de l'Union des associations culturelles pour le developpement de l'Ituri (UNADI), regroupant les 21 communautes de la province de l'Ituri. L'organisme estime, en effet, que les conditions sanitaires ne sont pas encore suffisamment rassurantes pour proceder a une rentree scolaire dans la region. C'est ce qui ressort de la reunion en assemblee generale extraordinaire, tenue le 30 août dernier a Bunia, lors de laquelle l'association avait appele a retarder la rentree pour le mois d'octobre prochain, un report qui devrait fournir plus de temps pour maîtriser la situation epidemiologique. Cite par le site d'information local Actualite.cd, le president de l'UNADI, Meta Wani Michel, a explique : « Nous ne remettons pas en cause l'importance de l'education. Notre preoccupation est d'abord sanitaire : avec Ebola, nous pensons qu'il faut prendre toutes les precautions pour eviter d'exposer les enfants, les enseignants et leurs familles ».

items.title: GH¢1.5m raised to renovate historic Wa Naa’s Palace
items.description: A fundraising gala in Wa has raised GH¢1.5 million in cash and pledges towards the refurbishment of the historic Wa Naa’s Palace and the construction of an ultra-modern conference facility within its precincts. The initiative, held at the Delagio Hotel in Wa, was organised under the auspices of Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin, who is also the Chief of Dakagli in the Waala State, in partnership with the Eco-Growth Development Initiatives Foundation. It forms part of the broader Royal Heritage and Inner-City Redevelopment Project, which seeks to preserve the palace’s traditional architecture while upgrading its facilities for contemporary administrative and cultural purposes. The event brought together traditional rulers, judicial officers, religious leaders, regional and local government officials and other stakeholders. A video documentary presented at the gala highlighted progress made on the multi-phase redevelopment project. The Chairman of the occasion, Supreme Court Justice Emmanuel Yonny Kulendi, pledged GH¢200,000 on behalf of himself, his law firm, Kulendi@Law, and associates. He described the palace as central to the identity and heritage of the people of Wa. “The Wa Naa’s Palace is more than just a residence; it is the soul of our people, the custodian of our history, and the courtroom of our peace,” Justice Kulendi said. He added that modern infrastructure was needed to enable traditional authorities to effectively conduct their administrative responsibilities and host visitors. The Secretary to the Wa Naa, Naa Kadir Ibrahim, who represented the Overlord of the Wala Traditional Area, Kuoro Sampou III, announced a personal contribution of GH¢200,000 from the Wa Naa. “Tonight is a statement of who we are. For generations, the palace has sheltered our identity, but today, it needs us to shelter it. You are not just donating to a building; you are investing in our shared heritage,” Naa Kadir said. The Upper West Regional Minister, Charles Lwanga Puozuing, said the redevelopment could contribute to tourism, job creation and investment in the region. “Modernity must serve heritage without destroying its soul. Cultural heritage is an economic asset capable of creating jobs, driving tourism, and attracting investment,” he said. On behalf of the Regional Coordinating Council and local government administration, Mr Puozuing announced a combined contribution of GH¢65,000, comprising GH¢10,000 from the Regional Coordinating Council and GH¢55,000 from Municipal and District Chief Executives across the region. The Catholic Bishop of the Wa Diocese, Most Rev. Francis Bomansaan, also commended the initiative and encouraged residents and members of the diaspora to support the redevelopment effort. Justice Kulendi, in closing the gala, said the fundraising campaign remained open to further contributions from corporate organisations and individuals. He assured donors that the project would be implemented with transparency, accountability and value for money. Historic palace The Wa Naa’s Palace is located in the heart of Wa and serves as the traditional seat of the Wa Naa, the Overlord of the Wala Traditional Area. The palace is recognised for its traditional mud-brick, Sudano-Sahelian architectural style, reflecting influences associated with the wider Sahel and Sudan regions. Beyond its role as a royal residence, the palace serves as an important centre for cultural, political, religious and social activities within the Waala traditional area. The redevelopment initiative is therefore aimed at preserving the palace’s heritage while providing facilities that can support the contemporary administrative and cultural functions of the traditional authority.

items.title: ‘Still a work in progress’ – Eric Tinkler admits Kotoko have plenty to improve
items.description: Asante Kotoko head coach Eric Tinkler says his side still have plenty of work to do despite their Democracy Cup victory over Hearts of Oak. The Kumasi giants secured a 4-1 victory on penalties following a goalless draw at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium, with goalkeeper Ibrahim Danlad making two crucial saves in the shootout. But Tinkler believes the victory is only an early step in the club’s rebuilding process. “When I first arrived, it wasn’t great,” he told the press. “But we’ve made strides going forward. The players that have come in have been received extremely well and they have integrated very quickly.” “But it’s still a work in progress, there’s still a lot of things that we need to improve on, in terms of synchronicity, understanding, philosophy, discipline and what I call the fundamentals.” The Porcupine Warriors begin their Ghana Premier League campaign on the road against newly promoted Debibi United on September 6 at the Golden City Park in Berekum. Kotoko have strengthened their squad during the transfer window with 12 new additions. Among the arrivals are the returning Danlad, Ivorian defender Koffi Marius Ange Bini, Burkina Faso midfielder Abdoul Kader Tarnagda, Cameroonian midfielder Solomon Nsor Asaah and Moroccan goalkeeper Abdel Wadie Mourad. Kotoko will hope the squad can help them improve on their eighth-place finish in the 2025/26 season.
